questions.stem: A young man presenting with features of recurrent brief depressive disorder, each lasting for about 3 to 7 days, for over a year. He had history of occasional headache and episodes of swooning attack in between, usually precipitated by emotional events. His neuroimaging revealed agenesis of corpus callosum. He was experiencing swooning attacks as he became aware that some ‘unusual’ findings were present in his reports. Recurrent brief depression can be a manifestation of this congenital anomaly, and conversion disorder can be present as comorbid diagnosis perhaps due to ignorance and fear of this apparently innocuous congenital malformation. What is blood supply of corpus callosum?

options.label: A
options.text: Anterior cerebral artery and middle cerebral artery

options.label: B
options.text: Anterior cerebral artery and posterior cerebral artery

options.label: C
options.text: Anterior cerebral artery and anterior communicating artery

options.label: D
options.text: Middle cerebral artery and posterior cerebral artery

questions.answerText: Anterior cerebral artery and anterior communicating artery
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Anterior cerebral artery and anterior communicating artery

 

There is controversy regarding this question - as per grays anatomy 42nd edition and recent research paper - Corpus callosum is supplied by pericallosal arteries and branches of anterior communicating arteries.


The pericallosal artery is formed by branches from anterior and posterior cerebral arteries (Mainly anterior cerebral artery). The part of the pericallosal artery which is derived from the anterior cerebral artery supplies the whole of corpus callosum, whereas the part of the pericallosal artery which supplies splenium is mainly derived from posterior cerebral artery.


Educational Objective:


If the question is asking about blood supply of corpus callosum the choice should be anterior cerebral artery and anterior communicating artery > anterior cerebral artery and posterior cerebral artery.


If the question is asking about the blood supply of anterior 4/5th of corpus callosum the answer will remain the same but if the question is about the blood supply of posterior 1/5th then the answer will be posterior cerebral artery as the first choice.

questions.stemHtml: A patient visited to orthopaedic OPD with complaint of Pain near the mid portion of the foot on the outside and bruising. His X Ray is shown in image where fracture has been observed at marked bone. What is your diagnosis?
Correct regarding given muscle in image:

options.label: A
options.text: I- Linea semilunaris, II- Linea alba, III – Inguinal ligament, IV- Inner lip of iliac crest

options.label: B
options.text: I- Linea alba, II- Arcuate ligament, III –Lacunar ligament, IV- Outer lip of iliac crest

options.label: C
options.text: I- Linea alba, II- Linea semilunaris, III – Inguinal ligament, IV- Inner lip of iliac crest

options.label: D
options.text: I- Linea alba, II- Linea semilunaris, III – Inguinal ligament, IV- Outer lip of iliac crest

questions.answerText: I- Linea alba, II- Linea semilunaris, III – Inguinal ligament, IV- Outer lip of iliac crest
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. I- Linea alba, II- Linea semilunaris, III – Inguinal ligament, IV- Outer lip of iliac crest

 

Linea alba - Is the midline of abdominal wall where insertion of muscles of anterior abdominal wall (external oblique, internal oblique and transverse abdominis) takes place.

 

Linea Semilunaris - The line which marks the lateral border of rectus abdominis.

 

Inguinal ligament - formed by the aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle. It extends from anterior superior iliac crest to the pubic tubercle.


Outer lip of iliac crest - The upper end of the iliac bone is called iliac crest. The anterior 2/3rd of the iliac crest is divided into three parts - outer lip, Inner lip and the intermediate part (between both the lips). The posterior 1/3rd of the iliac crest is divided into 2 parts - outer slope and inner slope.

A patient visited to casualty with history of head injury. On ICT examination it was found to be raised. Which kind of the eye deviation may be found in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Medial squint

 

Explanation:


Raised intracranial tension (ICT) often compresses the abducens nerve (cranial nerve VI) because of its long intracranial course. The abducens nerve innervates the lateral rectus muscle, which moves the eyeball outward. When this nerve is compromised, the lateral rectus becomes paralyzed, and the unopposed action of the medial rectus (innervated by the oculomotor nerve) draws the eye inward—resulting in a medial squint. This is a recognized sign of increased ICT, especially following head injury.

 

Other Options
 

Option A. Lateral squint: Outward deviation occurs only if the medial rectus is weak or paralyzed, which is not the case in raised ICT. Instead, abducens nerve involvement causes medial deviation.


Option C. Eyeball deviation downward and laterally: This pattern is seen with other cranial nerve injuries (such as oculomotor nerve palsy) rather than increased ICT.


Option D. None: With significant ICT, eye deviation (medial squint) is commonly present due to cranial nerve VI involvement.

 

Educational Objective:


Raised ICP is often associated with palsy of CN 6 (Abducens nerve). 
The function of CN 6 is lateral movement of the eyeball by the help of lateral rectus muscle. In case of palsy of CN6 the medial rectus overpowers the lateral rectus and medial quint is observed.
 

Reference: Vishram Singh text book of Clinical anatomy. 3rd Edition.



erence: Vishram Singh text book of Clinical anatomy. 3rd Edition.

questions.stem: A patient visited with history of abnormal protrusion of tongue on one side. Also, he had loss of fine touch sensation & hemiplegia symptoms on opposite half of body. What is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Dejerine’s syndrome

 

Dejerine syndrome is medial medullary syndrome, which occurs because of thrombosis of vertebral artery(ies).

 

Clinical features include

  1. Damage to pyramid - leading to contralateral hemiplegia
  2. Damage to hypoglossal nuclei and nerve - Ipsilateral atrophy and paralysis of tongue
  3. Damage to media lemniscus - Contralateral proprioception and fine touch loss.

 

Other options:

 

Option A: Wallenberg syndrome - It is lateral medullary syndrome caused due to thrombosis of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery. Symptoms include 

  1. Involvement of spinothalamic tract - Contralateral loss of pain and temperature
  2. Involvement of spinal nucleus and tract of trigeminal - Ipsilateral loss of pain and temperature over face.
  3. Involvement of nucleus ambigus - Ipsilateral loss of motor supply to muscle of pharynx, larynx and palate.
  4. Involvement of inferior cerebellar peduncle - Ataxia (Ipsilateral)
  5. Involvement of reticular formation - horner syndrome.

 

Option C. Perinaud Syndrome - It is defined as a group of symptoms which occur due to compression of superior colliculus of midbrain. Commonly it occurs because of tumours of pineal gland which compress the superior colliculus. MAin clinical feature is loss of upward gaze.

 

Option D. Millard Gubler Syndrome - It is medial inferior pontine syndrome. It occurs because of lesion in lower pons mainly at the side of the pyramidal tract and the site from where the fibers of abducens and facial nerve are emerging. Symptoms include -

  1. Involvement of abducens nerve - ipsilateral medial squint.
  2. Involvement of facial nerve - Ipsilateral facial palsy
  3. Involvement of corticospinal tract (Pyramidal tract) - Contralateral hemiplegia.
     

These symptoms are commonly referred as Abducent alternating hemiplegia

questions.stem: Which of the following is not the part of dorsal part of diencephalon?
Largest organ of body:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Skin

 

Skin is the largest organ of the body.
 

Option A. Liver: The liver is the largest gland


Option C. Interstitium: The interstitium is a tissue space, not an organ, and thus cannot be considered the largest organ.

 

Option D. Brain: The brain is an essential organ but much smaller in size compared to the skin.

 

Educational Objective:


Skin is the largest organ and liver is the largest gland of the body.

questions.stem: Internal capsule consists of which type of fibres:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Projection fibre

 

Projectional fibers are the ones which connect the cerebral cortex to other parts of CNS.

 

Internal capsule, corona radiata, Fimbria and fornix are the examples of projectional fibers.

 

Other Options:
 

Option A. Associational fibers Connect different parts of the same cerebral hemisphere with one another.

 

Examples include uncinate fasciculus, cingulum, superior longitudinal bundle, inferior longitudinal bundle, fronto-occipiotal bundle.
 

Option B. Commissural Fibers - There are the fibers of white matter which connect the same parts of the two cerebral hemispheres with one another. 
 

Examples - Corpus callosum, Anterior commissure, posterior commissure, habenular commissure.

 

Educational Objective:


Associational fibers connect different parts of the same cerebral hemisphere with one another.


Commissural Fibers  are the fibers of white matter which connect the same parts of the two cerebral hemispheres with one another. 


Projectional fibers are the ones which connect the cerebral cortex to other parts of CNS.


Reference:


Textbook of Neuroanatomy. Vishram Singh 4th Edition
